description.narrative: Incorporated in 2021, Redcliffe Lifetech Private Limited (Redcliffe or the Company) is a fast-growing, pan-India diagnostics service provider operating through a hub-and-spoke model to deliver quality and affordable pathology and radiology services, with a focus on Tier II and Tier III cities. IFC is proposing an equity investment of up to US$30 million (INR equivalent) in Redcliffe to support the Company's growth plans, including acquisitions and capital expenditure (the Project).The Project represents an opportunity for IFC to support the expansion of a pan-India, omni-channel, integrated diagnostics and radiology platform, while improving access to quality diagnostic services for patients with non-communicable diseases (NCDs) in underserved markets.

The most significant expected project-level outcome is increased access to high-quality, affordable diagnostics in India. At the market level, the investment is expected to contribute to sustaining the development of Indias diagnostics market by augmenting and expanding Redcliffes digital-first, direct-to-consumer hub-and-spoke model of diagnostic services. As India's population has rapidly grown, so has its need to deliver high-quality healthcare services. While the performance of India's health system has improved, significant gaps remain in access to and the quality of healthcare. Communicable diseases like dengue fever and chikungunya are still widespread, while the burden of non-communicable diseases continues to rise. Greater investment in healthcare infrastructure, technology, and the workforce is needed. Redcliffe aims to address the gaps in access to diagnostics by providing affordable diagnostic tests through its digital-first front end and extensive lab network. The Project will support the Company's expansion by supporting its growth plans through financing the acquisition of regional diagnostic and radiology platforms and capital expenditure. The Projects efforts to acquire and augment these radiology companies and integrate them into its digital direct-to-consumer diagnostics model are expected to improve access to diagnostics in India, particularly in Tier II and Tier III cities. At the market level, the Project is expected to contribute to increasing the competitiveness of the diagnostics sector in India. By augmenting Redcliffe's business model with greater radiology capabilities through acquisition, the Project will help sustain the development of India's fragmented diagnostics market to consolidate, formalize while being affordable.
